items.title: Uncorrelated jointly Gaussian blocks are independent
items.statement: Assume AC. If a finite-dimensional jointly Gaussian vector is partitioned into blocks U and V and every cross-covariance between U and V is zero, then U and V are independent. Singular covariance matrices are allowed.

references.title: Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Section 3.10
J. R. Norris, Probability and Measure, Sections 8.1–8.2

items.title: Best linear forecast from a finite history
items.statement: For a weakly stationary real process X indexed by Z, integers n,h≥1, and its common mean μ, the finite-history best linear forecast of X_{n+h} is the unique almost-sure class minimizing squared L2 error over all classes represented by a0+Σ_{j=1}^n a_jX_j with real coefficients. It is an affine L2 projection and does not, without further hypotheses, assert equality with conditional expectation.

references.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis, Section 5.2
Nicolai Meinshausen, Time Series Analysis: Notes for the course HS 2022, Section 2.7

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the finite-history predictor class
items.statement: Let X be a weakly stationary real process and let n,h≥1. The affine L2 minimization defining the finite-history best linear forecast of X_{n+h} from X_1,…,X_n has a unique minimizing almost-sure class, even when the history covariance matrix is singular.

references.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis, Section 5.2
Nicolai Meinshausen, Time Series Analysis: Notes for the course HS 2022, Section 2.7

items.title: Durbin–Levinson forecast recursion
items.statement: Given m≥1 and the ACVF lags γ(0),…,γ(m) of a weakly stationary real process, with every leading Toeplitz covariance matrix Γ_k=(γ(i−j))_{i,j=1}^k positive definite for 1≤k≤m, recursively compute the one-step centered forecast coefficients φ_{k,j} and error variances ν_k. Initialize ν_0=γ(0), κ_1=γ(1)/ν_0, φ_{1,1}=κ_1, and ν_1=ν_0(1−κ_1²). For k=2,…,m set κ_k=[γ(k)−Σ_{j=1}^{k−1}φ_{k−1,j}γ(k−j)]/ν_{k−1}, set φ_{k,j}=φ_{k−1,j}−κ_kφ_{k−1,k−j} for 1≤j<k and φ_{k,k}=κ_k, and set ν_k=ν_{k−1}(1−κ_k²). Output all φ_k and ν_k.

references.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis, Section 5.5.1
Nicolai Meinshausen, Time Series Analysis: Notes for the course HS 2022, Section 2.7

items.title: Finite-history forecast equations and error variance
items.statement: Let X be weakly stationary with mean μ and ACVF γ, let n,h≥1, and define Y_i=X_{n+1−i}, Γ_{ij}=γ(i−j), and γ_h=(γ(h),…,γ(h+n−1))ᵀ. If Γ is nonsingular, the unique forecast coefficients satisfy a=Γ⁻¹γ_h, the best linear forecast is μ+Σ_i a_i(Y_i−μ), and its forecast-error variance is γ(0)−aᵀγ_h.

references.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis, Section 5.2
Nicolai Meinshausen, Time Series Analysis: Notes for the course HS 2022, Section 2.7

items.title: A Gaussian finite-history forecast is a conditional expectation
items.statement: Assume AC. In the setting of the finite-history forecast theorem, if (X_{n+h},X_n,…,X_1) is jointly multivariate normal, then the best linear forecast equals E[X_{n+h}|σ(X_1,…,X_n)] almost surely, including when the history covariance is singular.

references.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis, Section 5.2
Nicolai Meinshausen, Time Series Analysis: Notes for the course HS 2022, Section 2.7

items.title: Durbin–Levinson solves the successive prediction equations
items.statement: Let X be weakly stationary with mean μ and ACVF γ, and suppose Γ_k=(γ(i−j))_{i,j=1}^k is positive definite for each 1≤k≤m. For every k≤m, the algorithm's φ_k is the unique solution of Γ_kφ_k=(γ(1),…,γ(k))ᵀ, and ν_k is the variance of X_{t+1}−μ−Σ_{j=1}^kφ_{k,j}(X_{t+1−j}−μ), equal to γ(0)−(γ(1),…,γ(k))ᵀφ_k.

references.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis, Section 5.5.1
Nicolai Meinshausen, Time Series Analysis: Notes for the course HS 2022, Section 2.7

items.title: One-step and multistep forecasts for a causal AR(1)
items.statement: For a weakly stationary causal AR(1) process with |φ|<1 and centered finite-variance white noise, the finite-history forecast of X_{n+h} is μ+φ^h(X_n−μ), and its error variance is σ²Σ_{j=0}^{h−1}φ^{2j}.

items.title: A singular history covariance can have nonunique coefficients
items.statement: For the stationary process X_t=Z with Z uniform on {−1,1}, predicting X_3 from X_1,X_2 gives a singular history covariance matrix. The normal equations have many coefficient solutions, but all yield the same predictor Z and the unique predictor class.

items.title: A finite-history conditional mean can be nonlinear
items.statement: A strictly stationary three-state cycle has a one-step conditional mean given X_1 that is not affine in X_1, while its best affine forecast is −X_1/2.
